title: Bind PumpStation to pinned UNIIMENTE Kernel contracts without creating local authority
problem: PumpStation needs a real institutional boundary for identity, legal principal, grants, policy, budgets, commitment, receipts, and reconciliation without copying the Kernel or allowing local wallet sessions to become consequence authority.
baseline: PumpStation has local authentication, simulation decisions, founder stage records, and zero external effects, but it has no exact binding to the canonical UNIIMENTE Kernel source or proposal transport contract.

alternatives.name: Copy Kernel logic into PumpStation
alternatives.description: Reimplement identity, grants, policy, and consequence checks locally.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Fast local integration but creates a second constitutional authority and inevitable drift.
alternatives.revival_evidence: Never revive as active authority. Local code may only validate and refuse against pinned contracts.

alternatives.name: Use wallet identity as institutional authority
alternatives.description: Treat a signed wallet session as the actor, legal principal, and financial mandate.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Simple user experience but collapses authentication, legal responsibility, and capability authority into one unsafe primitive.
alternatives.revival_evidence: Never revive. Wallet control may remain one authentication signal only.

alternatives.name: Pinned proposal adapter with deny-all gateway
alternatives.description: Pin exact Kernel source, compile bounded proposals, and refuse every consequence until live Kernel identity and grants exist.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Preserves one authority source and testability but requires contract-lock maintenance and a later authenticated gateway.
alternatives.revival_evidence: Current preferred experiment. Promote only after companion Kernel registration and live shadow transport.

alternatives.name: Wait for a completed TypeScript Kernel SDK
alternatives.description: Do no integration work until the Kernel publishes its planned SDK.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Avoids adapter code but leaves PumpStation architecture disconnected and ownership ambiguous.
alternatives.revival_evidence: Replace the adapter when an approved SDK provides equal or stronger contracts and tests.

do_nothing_option.name: Do nothing
do_nothing_option.description: Keep PumpStation simulation-only and do not expose a Kernel proposal boundary.
do_nothing_option.tradeoffs: Preserves current safety but delays proof that PumpStation can become a governed Venture Cell.
do_nothing_option.revival_evidence: Choose if the pinned adapter creates split-brain authority or cannot remain fail-closed.

roles.name: Founder-Intent Steward
roles.analysis: The founder wants agents and community capital to work as one organized institution, but human sovereignty and one canonical authority path must remain intact.
roles.position: Support a proposal-only adapter and separate companion registration proposal.

roles.name: Systems Architect
roles.analysis: The Kernel contract lock, organ manifest, gateway interface, and deny-all default establish clear state and authority ownership without importing the Kernel runtime.
roles.position: Support with exact source hashes, strict schemas, and replaceability by a future SDK.

roles.name: Adversarial Reviewer
roles.analysis: A local adapter can be mistaken for the real Kernel, a stale lock can normalize obsolete rules, and a malicious gateway can attempt to return allow.
roles.position: Support only if every allow is locally denied while unregistered and all source or payload changes invalidate the proposal.

roles.name: Operator and Maintainer
roles.analysis: Pinned blobs and explicit status routes make drift observable, but two repositories and stacked PRs increase release coordination burden.
roles.position: Support with companion PR lineage, CI, rollback, and one future SDK migration path.

roles.name: Evidence and Welfare Guardian
roles.analysis: No local authentication, community vote, or founder-interface action should silently become authority to move money or expose participants.
roles.position: Support while all proposals remain nonexecuting and legal, security, receipt, and reconciliation evidence remain explicit missing gates.

evidence.claim: The adapter pins exact Kernel contract, authority, identity, policy, and Consequence-Gate source revisions.
The PumpStation manifest has Level 0 autonomy, zero budget, no external targets, and no self-activation.
Tests reject tampering, stale locks, invalid grants, stage skipping, and malicious allow responses.

counterevidence.claim: PumpStation is not registered in the pinned Kernel service identity registry.
The pinned Kernel TypeScript SDK is a placeholder and not a live client.
No live Kernel decision, grant, commit witness, receipt, reconciliation, or external outcome exists.

pass_1.intended_outcome: Make PumpStation structurally compatible with one canonical Kernel while preserving zero unauthorized external effects.
advantages: Exact source and contract lineage is machine-readable.
Wallet authentication is explicitly separated from workload identity and legal authority.
The adapter can compile proposals while remaining unable to authorize them.
Local grant checks only narrow or refuse authority.

disadvantages.description: A stale pinned contract set can drift from the current Kernel.
disadvantages.redesign: Bind every proposal to the lock hash and source commit; require new review on any changed blob.

disadvantages.description: Developers or users may mistake the adapter for a live Kernel connection.
disadvantages.redesign: Expose disconnected and unregistered status, deny every proposal, and label all responses nonexecuting.

disadvantages.description: A gateway implementation could return allow before registration or complete consequence evidence.
disadvantages.redesign: Convert all allow responses into local denials while the manifest remains proposed and unregistered.

disadvantages.description: The companion registration proposal could be confused with active identity or grant issuance.
disadvantages.redesign: Keep it outside the active registry, status INACTIVE, approval NOT_REQUESTED, budget zero, and test that no active identity exists.

disadvantages.description: Cross-repository updates can create release-order and rollback complexity.
disadvantages.redesign: Use independent draft PRs, exact source references, no automatic merge, and a future SDK replacement path.

rejected_alternatives.name: Activate PumpStation in the Kernel registry immediately
rejected_alternatives.description: Add the identity and issue a capability grant in the same change.
rejected_alternatives.tradeoffs: Would accelerate integration but bypass manifest hash binding, security review, legal-principal confirmation, and founder approval.
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: Only after all registration-proposal approvals are independently satisfied.

rejected_alternatives.name: Permit internal simulation writes from a local allow
rejected_alternatives.description: Treat low consequence as sufficient for local execution authority.
rejected_alternatives.tradeoffs: Convenient but establishes a second consequence path and weakens the one-Kernel invariant.
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: No revival; internal durable writes should still be attributable and governed.

new_weaknesses: The adapter contract mirrors Kernel concepts but is not generated from an official SDK.
The lock verifies declared SHAs but does not fetch and cryptographically verify remote blobs at runtime.
The companion PR is inactive and therefore does not prove service-to-service interoperability.
Proposal denial alone does not test commit-time revalidation or receipt reconciliation.

disadvantage_dispositions.action: Retain the lock until an official SDK or automated source-verification job replaces it.
Status and API responses explicitly report disconnected, unregistered, and no execution authority.
A malicious allow fixture is converted to denial and covered by tests.
The Kernel proposal remains outside the active registry and includes tests proving inactivity.
Keep both PRs draft and establish merge order only after exact manifest hash approval.

pass_2.strengthened_design: Retain a pinned, proposal-only, deny-all adapter as the Phase 3 sandbox boundary. Keep PumpStation unregistered, preserve a separate inactive Kernel registration proposal, and require exact manifest approval before any shadow transport or grant issuance.
residual_risks: No live authenticated Kernel transport exists.
No official generated TypeScript SDK exists.
No active service identity or grant exists.
No commit witness, effect receipt, or reconciliation has been exercised.

dissent.position: Wait for the official TypeScript SDK instead of maintaining a handwritten adapter.
dissent.rationale: Mirrored types can drift and increase maintenance burden.
dissent.evidence_threshold: Replace the adapter when the official SDK covers proposals, grants, decisions, receipts, and source-version negotiation with equal tests.
dissent.review_trigger: Any official SDK release or Kernel contract-version change.

dissent.position: Do not register PumpStation until an independent security review and legal-principal confirmation are complete.
dissent.rationale: Identity registration can create organizational legitimacy even before a grant is issued.
dissent.evidence_threshold: Approved manifest hash, security report, legal-principal record, and explicit founder registration decision.
dissent.review_trigger: Any proposal to modify the active Kernel service identity registry.

authority_impact: None. PumpStation remains unregistered, zero-budget, Level 0, proposal-only, disconnected, and unable to execute external effects.
migration_plan: Keep this stacked draft behind Phase 2. Review the companion inactive Kernel registration proposal separately. Replace handwritten contracts with the official Kernel SDK when available.
rollback_plan: Close PR #15 or revert its commits. Phase 2 remains independently reviewable and the canonical Kernel registry remains unchanged.
kill_criteria: Any local adapter result creates execution authority.
Wallet authentication is treated as workload identity or legal mandate.
PumpStation enters the active Kernel registry without the required approvals.
A changed proposal, source revision, or contract lock remains valid.
A simulate grant authorizes a financial, external, or irreversible consequence.
review_trigger: Official Kernel SDK, contract revision, companion registration review, or any proposal to enable shadow transport.
